battle.name: 圖阿雷格叛亂 (1990年-1995年)
battle.theater: 馬利北部蒂姆巴克圖地區
battle.brief: 圖阿雷格叛亂於1990年3月在馬利北部爆發，圖阿雷格武裝與馬利政府軍交戰，衝突延續至1995年。同期海軍裝備中的 Torpedo boat 於1877年已在英國海軍服役，屬早期快速水面兵力，適合沿岸警戒、追擊與反艦任務，是近海防衛體系的一部分。

kit.name: 魚雷艇
kit.history: Torpedo boat 是英國海軍早期魚雷作戰艇種，1877年投入近海與港口防衛，以高速執行警戒、攔截及反艦任務，屬於早期海軍快速反水面的作戰兵力。

countries: 1990年4月，戰場集中在馬利共和國北部的薩赫勒沙漠。政府的權力中心在南方邦馬庫，北面則以廷巴克圖、加奧、吉達爾、門納卡四個據點維持道路與機場；廷巴克圖至加奧約四百公里，再向東北可進入阿德雷爾與伊福加斯山區。開戰者並非一個獲國際承認的政府，而是數個圖阿雷格武裝運動，它們以「阿扎瓦德」為共同政治名稱，主張北部脫離馬利，但阿扎瓦德從未成為受國際承認的國家。馬利政府軍以南方為後方，控制主要公路和較大的城鎮；法國則在1993年才應邀提供空運、空中支援與有限地面兵力。毛里塔尼亞與尼日爾同期也有各自的圖阿雷格衝突，不能與馬利戰線混作同一支軍隊，然而三國邊境的人員、武器、消息與作戰經驗確實互相流動。
countriesEn: In April 1990, the theater was the Saharan desert in northern Mali. The government’s center of power lay at Bamako in the south, while Timbuktu, Gao, Kidal, and Ménaka served as the principal northern centers for roads and airfields. Timbuktu and Gao are roughly four hundred kilometers apart, with the Adrar and Ifoghas mountain regions lying farther to the northeast. The insurgents were not an internationally recognized government but several Tuareg armed movements that used Azawad as a common political designation and sought the separation of northern Mali from the southern state. Azawad was never internationally recognized as a country. Malian government forces operated from the south and controlled the main roads and larger towns, while France provided airlift, air support, and a limited ground presence only after being invited in 1993. Mauritania and Niger also experienced their own Tuareg conflicts during this period; those forces cannot be treated as part of the Malian front, although personnel, weapons, information, and combat experience moved across all three border zones.
people: 直接觸發事件發生在1990年4月9日：加奧一批隸屬政府軍的圖阿雷格士兵遭殺害；後來敘述對命令責任、確切經過與死亡人數並不一致，本紀錄不採單一精確傷亡數字。5月16日，若干圖阿雷格派別宣布阿扎瓦德獨立，十餘日內的攻勢把門納卡、廷巴克圖及加奧外圍的政府據點逐個捲入衝突。伊亞德·阿格·加利於1990年組織阿扎瓦德解放運動，1991年成為阿扎瓦德協調組織的核心領導人；其他武裝派別仍保有各自的指揮與談判管道，並沒有一條統一全線的圖阿雷格總參謀部。總統穆薩·特拉奧雷最初以軍事手段鎮壓，1991年3月底政變後，由阿爾法·烏馬爾·科納雷主持的政府接續談判；阿馬杜·圖馬尼·圖雷自1992年出任馬利陸軍參謀長，負責北部防務以及1993年的法軍協同作戰。阿爾及利亞政府後來提供會談場所，並分別接觸不同派別。
peopleEn: The immediate triggering event occurred on 9 April 1990, when a group of Tuareg soldiers serving in the Malian army were killed at Gao. Later accounts differ concerning command responsibility, the precise sequence of events, and the number of dead, so this record does not assign a single exact casualty figure. On 16 May, several Tuareg factions declared Azawad independent, and an offensive over the following days drew Ménaka, Timbuktu, and government positions around Gao into the conflict. Iyad Ag Ghali organized the Azawad Liberation Movement in 1990 and became the central leader of the Azawad Coordination in 1991. Other armed factions retained separate commands and negotiating channels, and there was no unified Tuareg general staff controlling the entire front. President Moussa Traoré initially relied on military suppression. Following the coup at the end of March 1991, the government headed by Alpha Oumar Konaré continued negotiations. Amadou Toumani Touré became chief of the Malian army staff in 1992 and directed northern defense and cooperation with French forces in 1993. The Algerian government later provided a venue for talks and made direct contact with the separate factions.
kits: 馬利政府軍以蘇制AK-47、AKM與SKS步槍為主，配備PKM通用機槍、RPG-7火箭筒及少量D-30 122毫米牽引榴砲，坦克則有數量不多的T-34-85；後勤車隊使用重型卡車與Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60四輪驅動車。圖阿雷格初起時多靠步槍、手槍與RPG-7，奪取軍械庫後取得AKM、PKM、7.62毫米機槍與可用車輛，再以Toyota Hilux皮卡加裝DShK 12.7毫米重機槍構成技術車，亦使用Land Rover 101與FJ60巡邏、載員及運送彈藥。彈藥消耗集中在7.62×39毫米、7.62×54毫米R、40毫米火箭彈及砲彈；油料以標準汽油桶與備用油箱攜帶，輪胎、工具、無線電與維修件決定技術車能持續移動多遠。法軍在1993年投入VAB裝甲運兵車、AMX-30坦克、C-160 Transall運輸機及Mirage F1戰鬥機；美軍「Barras」空運則使用C-141 Starlifter與C-130 Hercules。所述型號在1990年底前均已列裝。
kitsEn: Malian government forces centered their infantry equipment on Soviet AK-47, AKM, and SKS rifles, supported by PKM general-purpose machine guns, RPG-7 launchers, and a small number of D-30 122 mm towed howitzers. Their tanks included a limited number of T-34-85s, while heavy trucks and Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60 four-wheel-drive vehicles formed the logistics fleet. The Tuareg initially relied on rifles, pistols, and RPG-7 launchers. After seizing army depots, they obtained AKMs, PKMs, 7.62 mm machine guns, and usable vehicles. They then mounted DShK 12.7 mm heavy machine guns on Toyota Hilux pickups to form technicals, while Land Rover 101s and FJ60s were used for patrols, troop transport, and ammunition movement. Ammunition expenditure centered on 7.62×39 mm, 7.62×54 mmR, 40 mm rockets, and artillery shells. Fuel was carried in standard drums and auxiliary tanks, while tires, tools, radios, and repair parts determined how far a technical could continue operating. In 1993, French forces brought in VAB armored personnel carriers, AMX-30 tanks, C-160 Transall transports, and Mirage F1 fighters. American Operation Barras used C-141 Starlifter and C-130 Hercules transports. Every type named here had entered service before the end of 1990.
tactics: 1990年5月的第一波攻勢採取小規模突擊、快速轉移與奪取固定目標的作法。圖阿雷格戰鬥組以技術車和徒步分隊在夜間接近據點，白天攻擊無線電站、軍械庫及政府機關，得到武器後立即分散，避免在城鎮外圍留下可供政府軍集中攻擊的固定陣地。政府軍則沿RN1公路反擊，縱隊由邦馬庫經塞古、莫普提、傑內前往廷巴克圖，再向加奧推進；裝甲車、牽引砲、燃料車與護衛車組成長距離車隊，前後距離因伏擊而拉開。圖阿雷格在公路上設置障礙、襲擊燃料與彈藥車，以RPG-7對付坦克，以重機槍射擊卡車，隨即退回山區。政府軍能重新奪取主要公路城鎮，卻難以長期搜索分散的游擊隊。1991年政變造成北方的權力空隙，圖阿雷格再向加奧與吉達爾方向推進，切斷部分道路並包圍若干孤立據點。1993年法軍以空襲、空運與裝甲地面協同奪取加奧一帶的機場和道路軸線，再由馬利部隊接替地面控制；這種作戰迫使武裝力量避免與法軍正面對抗，但無法清除整片山區，遂使軍事優勢轉化為談判壓力。
tacticsEn: The first offensive of May 1990 relied on small assault groups, rapid movement, and the seizure of fixed objectives. Tuareg combat teams approached positions at night in technicals and on foot, struck radio stations, weapons depots, and government installations during the day, and dispersed as soon as weapons were obtained so that government forces could not concentrate against a fixed formation. The government answered along National Route 1, moving convoys from Bamako through Ségou, Mopti, and Djenné to Timbuktu and onward toward Gao. Armored vehicles, towed artillery, fuel trucks, and escorts formed long columns whose spacing expanded when an ambush stopped the lead vehicles. The Tuareg obstructed roads, attacked fuel and ammunition vehicles, used RPG-7 launchers against tanks and heavy machine guns against trucks, and then withdrew into mountain terrain. Government forces could retake the principal road towns but could not comb isolated dispersed guerrilla bands. The 1991 coup created a political vacuum in the north, allowing another Tuareg drive toward Gao and Kidal, the cutting of roads, and the encirclement of isolated positions. In 1993, French air attacks, air landings, and armored ground operations secured airfields and the road axis around Gao before Malian units assumed control of the ground. This forced the armed groups to avoid direct confrontation with French forces, but it could not clear the mountain regions. The military advantage therefore became pressure for negotiations.
data: 可核對的時間線始於1990年4月9日的加奧事件，隨後是5月16日宣布阿扎瓦德獨立；5月下旬至6月初，圖阿雷格一度奪取或襲擊數個城鎮，馬利政府的反擊則重新控制廷巴克圖、加奧等主要公路節點。1991年3月底政變後，北方攻勢再度擴張，圖阿雷格武裝曾進入或包圍加奧與吉達爾，但政府仍保有邦馬庫及通往南方的補給線。1992年的停火接觸沒有形成可持續執行的安排。1993年1月15日至2月21日，法軍執行Operation Épervier，約五百名法軍人員配合馬利陸軍恢復北部交通；同月美國Operation Barras以C-141與C-130把物資從幾內亞的空運點送至邦馬庫。1994年4月4日，馬利政府與阿扎瓦德協調組織在阿爾及爾簽署和平協定。1995年仍有零星衝突、武器繳交與派系間的補充執行協議，但大規模攻城與縱隊戰已逐漸停止。各次戰鬥的傷亡數字彼此矛盾，加奧事件尤其缺乏一致的原始紀錄；整場衝突也沒有跨年度、可核對的總傷亡表，因此不能把零散數字拼成精確總數。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology begins with the incident at Gao on 9 April 1990, followed by the declaration of Azawad independence on 16 May. From late May to early June, the Tuareg seized or attacked several towns, while government counteroffensives regained major road centers such as Timbuktu and Gao. After the coup at the end of March 1991, the northern offensive expanded again, and Tuareg forces entered or surrounded Gao and Kidal, although the government retained Bamako and the supply route leading south. Ceasefire contacts in 1992 failed to produce a workable settlement. From 15 January to 21 February 1993, France conducted Operation Épervier, deploying approximately five hundred personnel alongside Malian troops to restore communications in the north. American Operation Barras used C-141 and C-130 aircraft during the same month to move supplies from an airlift point in Guinea to Bamako. On 4 April 1994, the Malian government and the Azawad Coordination signed a peace agreement in Algiers. Sporadic fighting, weapons surrender, and supplementary implementation arrangements continued during 1995, but large-scale urban sieges and convoy battles progressively ended. Casualty accounts for individual actions conflict with one another, and the original record for the Gao incident is especially inconsistent. No verified, multi-year casualty ledger exists for the conflict as a whole, so isolated figures cannot be combined into a precise total.
cause: 這場叛亂不能只歸因於一次乾旱或一次軍事事件。長期因素包括1963年至1964年叛亂留下的未解決記憶，以及圖阿雷格人雖被大量徵入馬利軍隊，卻在軍官晉升、裝備配給與政治職位上持續感到受排斥。1970年代以後的乾旱、國家對牧場與水源的重新編組，以及商路控制權向南方行政中心集中，也削弱了北部傳統勢力的經濟基礎。殖民時期劃定的邊界把圖阿雷格分布區切分在馬利、尼日爾與阿爾及利亞之間，武器、婚姻網與消息沿邊境往來；1989年至1990年的毛里塔尼亞衝突又提供了武裝經驗。1990年4月9日加奧的殺害事件是直接爆發點，特拉奧雷政府以軍事清剿回應，使原本分散的不滿迅速匯聚成共同行動。1991年政變削弱中央控制後，北方進攻得到更大空間；法國介入則證明政府若要恢復北部公路，必需外部空中與後勤協助。阿爾及利亞的介入則為雙方建立談判頻道，使軍事僵局最終轉向阿爾及爾的正式協議。
causeEn: The rebellion cannot be reduced to either drought or a single military incident. Long-term causes included the unresolved memory of the 1963–64 uprising and the persistent sense that Tuareg soldiers, although recruited in large numbers into the Malian army, remained disadvantaged in officer promotion, equipment allocation, and political appointments. Drought from the 1970s onward, state reorganization of pastures and water sources, and the concentration of trade-route control in southern administrative centers weakened the economic foundation of northern power networks. Colonial borders divided Tuareg territories among Mali, Niger, and Algeria, while weapons, kinship networks, and information moved across those borders. The Mauritanian conflict of 1989–90 also supplied armed experience. The killing of Tuareg soldiers at Gao on 9 April 1990 was the immediate flashpoint, and Traoré’s decision to answer it with military sweeps caused separate grievances to merge into a coordinated movement. The 1991 coup further reduced central control and gave the northern offensive room to expand. French involvement later demonstrated that restoring the northern roads required outside air and logistical assistance, while Algerian mediation created the diplomatic channel that finally turned a military stalemate into the Algiers agreement.
impact: 作戰層面的第一個影響，是雙方都發現控制幾座城鎮不等於控制北部。圖阿雷格可以憑速度奪取加奧、廷巴克圖與吉達爾周邊，卻因補給、固守和通信不足而無法長期占據；馬利政府軍雖能重奪公路，傳統的分散搜索也難以清除山區游擊隊。法國直接投入空中與裝甲力量，迅速改變了1993年的戰術平衡，也同時暴露馬利遠程補給和沙漠機動能力不足。往後數年，馬利陸軍更重視分隊護衛、連續補給、先進偵察與外國訓練，北部防衛也由單純守住據點轉向依託道路、空軍支援及地方情報網。政治上，政府不能只靠奪回城市維持統一，必須在北部行政權、軍隊整合與政治代表安排上作出讓步。阿扎瓦德協調組織則從鬆散武裝聯盟變為能簽署協議、調度資金與維持邊境網絡的長期政治軍事力量，其武裝經驗與未完全解除的武器庫，後來成為2006年至2007年新一輪衝突的重要基礎。這些影響並不等於雙方原有的制度與邊界爭議已被解決。
impactEn: The first operational consequence was that neither side could equate control of several towns with control of the north. The Tuareg could use speed to seize Gao, Timbuktu, and positions around Kidal, but weak logistics, garrison requirements, and communications prevented them from holding those towns indefinitely. Malian government forces could recover the roads, but conventional dispersed searches proved inadequate against guerrilla bands in the mountains. Direct French air and armored intervention quickly changed the tactical balance in 1993 while also exposing Mali’s weaknesses in long-range supply and desert mobility. In subsequent years, the Malian army placed greater emphasis on convoy protection, continuous logistics, advance reconnaissance, and foreign training. Northern defense increasingly combined roads, air support, and local intelligence networks rather than reliance on isolated garrisons. Politically, the government could not preserve unity merely by retaking cities; it had to make concessions concerning northern administration, military integration, and political representation. The Azawad Coordination developed from a loose alliance into a durable political and military organization capable of signing agreements, moving funds, and maintaining cross-border networks. Its combat experience and incompletely secured weapons caches later became important foundations for the renewed conflict of 2006–07. These changes did not, however, resolve the institutional and border disputes that had produced the original war.
result: 1994年4月4日，馬利政府與阿扎瓦德協調組織在阿爾及爾簽署《阿爾及爾和平協定》。協定要求停止敵對行動，由北方運動交出武器並解散大部分武裝，戰士可按程序進入馬利軍警或行政體系；北方則取得特殊行政地位與較大的地方治理權。這不是馬利放棄加奧、廷巴克圖與吉達爾的主權，也不是阿扎瓦德獲得國際承認。1995年，未簽署或拒絕完整執行的派別另行接受補充安排，凡交出武器者移往加奧附近指定集結營點，部分武裝被納入政府控制，另有戰士選擇加入軍警或維持未武裝的武裝生活；因此零星衝突與違約事件仍曾出現。到1995年底，大規模攻城和縱隊戰已停止，阿扎瓦德協調組織的主要武裝完成集結或解散，北部主要城鎮、機場和道路恢復政府控制，協議則成為雙方處理軍事與政治問題的基本框架。無法核實的精確傷亡總數不應被補造；可以確定的是，1990年占領城市的軍事成果未能持久，而政府保住疆域後，仍以行政讓步、軍隊整合和國際協助換取停火。協議留下的武器登錄、北方權限與武裝復原問題沒有完全消失，並在2006年至2007年的新一輪衝突中重新顯現。
resultEn: On 4 April 1994, the Malian government and the Azawad Coordination signed the Algiers Peace Accord. The agreement required a cessation of hostilities, the surrender of weapons and dissolution of most armed formations by the northern movement, and allowed fighters to enter the Malian military, police, or administrative services through established procedures. It also granted the north a special administrative status and a larger role in local government. Mali did not relinquish sovereignty over Gao, Timbuktu, or Kidal, and Azawad did not receive international recognition. During 1995, factions that had not signed or had refused full implementation accepted supplementary arrangements. Those who surrendered weapons were moved to designated cantonment sites near Gao; some formations entered government control, while other fighters joined the military or police or maintained an unarmed military role. Sporadic clashes and violations therefore continued for part of the year. By the end of 1995, major sieges and convoy battles had stopped, the principal Tuareg formations had either cantoned or disarmed, and government control of the principal northern towns, airfields, and roads had been restored. The agreement became the basic framework for subsequent military and political arrangements. No exact overall casualty total should be invented because none can be verified. What can be established is that the military gains of 1990 did not endure, and that the government retained the territory only by exchanging a ceasefire for administrative concessions, military integration, and outside assistance. Problems involving weapons registration, northern authority, and the reconstitution of armed groups remained unresolved and later reappeared in the renewed conflict of 2006–07.
